adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — The matcher rejects only a mismatching substring and otherwise accepts any grant shortcut, so grant-context regressions pass silently.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the matcher code at line 483: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` - this logic is inverted. It returns false (rejects) when the grant shortcut MATCHES the expected value, and returns true (accepts) when it doesn't match. The correct logic should be `if (!items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` to reject non-matching shortcuts. This means the test will pass even when the grant shortcut is wrong, silently allowing grant-context regressions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Adding an abstract getShortcut method breaks pre-existing external grant-provider binaries at startup with AbstractMethodError.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface (in server-spi-private) adds a new abstract method `getShortcut()` without a default implementation. This is a breaking change for any existing external implementations of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory that were compiled against the previous version of the interface. When those implementations are loaded at runtime, they will fail with AbstractMethodError because they don't implement the new required method. The interface is in a 'spi' package suggesting it's meant for extension by external providers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:105 — Removing the public Context copy constructor breaks deployed grant extensions that clone request contexts with NoSuchMethodError.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the removal of the copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` from lines 102-116 in OAuth2GrantType.java. This constructor was previously public and part of the API. If any external grant extensions (deployed as plugins/providers) were using this copy constructor to clone request contexts, they would now fail with NoSuchMethodError at runtime since the method no longer exists. This is a binary compatibility break for the SPI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Adding required getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2 grant provider binaries at startup when postInit invokes it

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface without a default implementation. In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()`, the code iterates over all `OAuth2GrantType` provider factories and calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on each one. Any existing third-party implementations of `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` that haven't been recompiled with this new method will throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime when `postInit` is called during startup. This is a binary compatibility break that would cause startup failures for deployments with custom grant type providers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:87 — Removing the public Context(Context) constructor breaks custom grant providers compiled against the prior SPI

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the removal of the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor (lines 102-115 in the old code are deleted). This constructor was part of the public SPI interface `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. Any custom grant type providers that were compiled against the previous version and used this copy constructor would fail at runtime with a NoSuchMethodError when upgraded to this new version. This is a binary compatibility break in a public SPI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1054 — Access-token jti values are no longer UUIDs, breaking UUID-parsing consumers without a compatibility or version boundary

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that token IDs are now encoded with a prefix format (e.g., 'onrtac:UUID' as seen in the test file DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java). The encodeTokenId method in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java creates IDs like 'sessionType.shortcut + tokenType.shortcut + grantShortcut + ':' + rawTokenId'. This is a real architectural change that could break external consumers expecting pure UUIDs. The test file confirms the new format with assertions like 'trltcc:1234' and 'ofrtro:5678'. However, this appears to be an intentional design change with the new TokenContextEncoderSpi, not a bug. It's an important compatibility concern but represents a deliberate API change rather than a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — The matcher rejects the expected grant shortcut, so every updated token-id expectation fails for correctly encoded tokens.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — A custom grant shortcut not exactly two characters can mint an ID that this parser always rejects, despite the factory contract describing three-letter shortcuts.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real inconsistency. In OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java, the Javadoc says shortcuts are 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but the parser in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 hardcodes exactly 6 characters for the encoded context (2 for sessionType + 2 for tokenType + 2 for grantType), and all actual implementations use 2-character shortcuts (e.g., 'ac', 'cc', 'rt'). If someone follows the Javadoc and creates a 3-letter shortcut, the encoding would be 7 characters, but the parser at line 74 checks 'encodedContext.length() != 6' and would reject it. This is a documentation/contract mismatch that could cause runtime failures for custom grant implementations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Existing external grant factories lack the newly mandatory method and will throw AbstractMethodError during provider post-init, preventing the server from starting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:112 — Dynamically discovered grant shortcuts overwrite existing mappings without collision validation, so a later provider can corrupt token-context decoding for an already active grant.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java lines 108-115 (getShortcutByGrantType method), when a new grant type is dynamically discovered, it calls `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` and `grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut)` without checking if the shortcut already exists in the map. This means if a newly deployed provider has the same shortcut as an existing grant, it will silently overwrite the mapping. The postInit method (lines 66-79) does validate for duplicates at startup, but the dynamic discovery in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut (lines 120-133) does not perform this validation. This could corrupt token decoding for existing grants if a malicious or buggy provider is deployed with a duplicate shortcut.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74 — Grant shortcuts are not validated as non-null two-character values, allowing a custom provider to crash initialization or issue token IDs that the decoder rejects.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java lines 68-77, the postInit method iterates over OAuth2GrantType factories and calls getShortcut() on each, storing results in maps. There's no validation that shortcuts are non-null or exactly 2 characters. The decoder in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java lines 69-87 expects exactly 6 characters in the encoded context (2 for sessionType + 2 for tokenType + 2 for grantType), using substring operations. If a custom provider returns null or a shortcut of wrong length, this would cause either NullPointerException during encoding or incorrect parsing during decoding. The finding correctly identifies a missing validation that could cause runtime failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:40 — The codec tests seed private maps and use a null session, leaving production SPI discovery and issuance-time context derivation untested.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the unit test in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java manually seeds the factory's maps (grantsByShortcuts, grantsToShortcuts) and passes null for the session parameter. This means the test doesn't exercise the actual SPI discovery mechanism in postInit() that populates these maps from OAuth2GrantType providers, nor does it test getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() which requires a real session. However, this is a valid testing approach for unit tests - it isolates the encoding/decoding logic. The finding is technically accurate but represents a scope concern about test coverage rather than a bug. Integration tests would be needed to verify the full SPI wiring.
